sum: Three easy days east of Kathmandu: sunrise at Nagarkot, a ridge and village walk to Dhulikhel, then on to the stupa and monastery at Namobuddha and down to the old town of Panauti.

guide.note: This walk lies outside the national parks and conservation areas. There is no permit and no checkpost, and nobody asks for a guide. One is still worth hiring for the Nagarkot to Dhulikhel day, where new dirt roads fork every few hundred metres and nothing is signed, and for anyone who would otherwise walk the quiet forest sections alone.

access: Both ends are a short ride from Kathmandu. Nagarkot is about 32 km east of the city: an hour and a half to two hours by taxi, or up to three hours by local bus with a change in Bhaktapur. From Panauti, frequent buses run to Kathmandu by way of Banepa in about an hour and a half. Dhulikhel is on the Araniko Highway, with buses all day if you need to cut the walk short. Namobuddha has only a few buses, so most walkers who stop there book a car.

photo.a: Strings of colourful prayer flags radiate from the spire of a whitewashed stupa, which is ringed by smaller stupas and a rail of prayer wheels, under a blue sky with white clouds.

tips: Nagarkot and Dhulikhel fill with weekenders from Kathmandu. Walk midweek, or book both hotels ahead for a Friday or Saturday night.
Ask your Nagarkot hotel for a packed lunch. Tea shops between the tower and Dhulikhel are few and keep irregular hours.
Leave your main bag in Kathmandu. With a hotel every night you need only a day pack with a warm layer and a head torch for the dawn.
At Namobuddha, walk clockwise round the stupa, dress modestly in the monastery and ask before photographing monks or shrine rooms.
Dhulikhel and Panauti have cash machines. Carry small notes for tea shops, buses and temple donations.

days.note: Leave Kathmandu after lunch and you reach Nagarkot in time for the sunset. Most hotels sit well below the 2,175 m usually quoted for the village, which is the height of the view-tower hill to the south. Eat early and set an alarm: the dawn is why you are here.

After sunrise, follow the ridge road south to the view tower and take the forest path down to the saddle of Rohini Bhanjyang. From there dirt roads and village paths lead through Kankre, Tanchok and Opi to the Araniko Highway just short of Dhulikhel. Ask the way in every village.

days.t: Dhulikhel to Namobuddha and Panauti, drive to Kathmandu
days.note: Climb the long flight of steps to the Kali temple, drop to the highway at Kavre Bhanjyang and follow a dirt road through Phulbari to Namobuddha, three to four hours in all. After the stupa and the monastery, walk down through Sankhu and Sunthan to Panauti in under three hours and take the bus to Kathmandu.
